headline: Your Swimm waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing engineering orgs into the right Swimm modernization offer. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Omer Rosenbaum, Co-Founder & CTO.
productSummary: Swimm is a product-enabled service company, not a self-serve license. They combine proprietary deterministic static analysis, GenAI for scale, and senior engineers who catch what tools miss, then deliver the change: migrated code, extracted APIs, or an AI-ready knowledge base. Three homepage offers: API-first architecture, an agentic context layer for Copilot / Cursor / Claude Code / MCP, and large-scale migrations (.NET, Java, monolith to microservices, plus COBOL / JCL / PL/I mainframe). Engagements run Assessment, Specification, Modernization, Enablement. Fixed price, with validation evidence at every step. SOC 2 and ISO 27001, on-prem and air-gapped, customer-managed LLMs.
coreInsight: Omer already sells agentic modernization against codebases AI tools cannot safely touch. The one TAM is engineering organizations LinkedIn already lists. The one routing signal is the modernization keyword sitting in their open job posts, because Sales Nav returns that keyword in the same pull and it tells you whether they are staffing a mainframe estate, an active stack migration, an AI-coding-tool rollout, or none of those yet.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is the keyword already in the job post
sections.takeaway: LinkedIn already names the engineering org and already prints COBOL, WebForms, Struts, or Copilot in the open req. That keyword is stronger than a headcount guess, and it is free to collect.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes every engineering org
sections.takeaway: First match wins. Mainframe keywords go first, then active migration keywords, then AI-coding-tool keywords, then every remaining in-TAM engineering org.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Each job keyword gets a different first offer
sections.takeaway: Mainframe hiring gets a parity brief. Stack-migration hiring gets a pattern map. Copilot/Cursor hiring gets a context-gap one-pager. The rest get an AI-readiness assessment snapshot.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: Parity, ship the last 40%, make Copilot useful, on the same routes
sections.takeaway: The list is always engineering orgs, aimed at CTO / VP Eng / Head of Architecture / CIO. Industry and stack name are merge tags, not a second TAM. A/Bs sit on the exclusive routes.

sections.label: Email Copy
sections.title: Copy that names the stack they already posted
sections.takeaway: Notice the req, poke the spec-that-lives-in-the-code problem that keyword implies, then ask for a one-letter yes.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the mainframe keyword first
sections.takeaway: Start where they are already hiring against COBOL, JCL, or PL/I. Prove reply density, then roll migration, AI-tool, and the AI-readiness catch-all.

signalReasons: LinkedIn Sales Nav job search is the TAM Swimm's own pages sell into, engineering orgs with a visible software team, and the modernization keyword in one pull.

The same pull returns COBOL / JCL / PL/I, WebForms / VB.NET / Struts / EJB / WebSphere, monolith-to-microservices, API-first / headless, or Copilot / Cursor / Claude Code, which is enough to route without a second enrichment product.
The ladder maps to live Swimm copy: mainframe parity, large-scale .NET / Java / monolith / API-first migrations, the agentic context layer, and the remaining AI-readiness gap Maya already pitched.
Industry and title are a scrape filter. They are not a second waterfall.

tiers.name: Tier 1
tiers.label: Mainframe keyword
tiers.trigger: LinkedIn job post names COBOL, JCL, PL/I, CICS, DB2, IMS, or mainframe
tiers.pain: Decades of COBOL, JCL, PL/I, and DB2 carry the rules of the business. Logic lives in thousands of programs with no spec to migrate against. Auto-translators produce code that compiles; the business does not run the same. Swimm's 2.0 post: Claude Code on a government COBOL codebase hit 35% coverage, 70% accuracy, and 42% variance between runs.
tiers.valueProp: Deterministic analysis of the complete COBOL / PL/I / JCL / DB2 / copybook estate, then verified migration patterns with SME validation and parity evidence. Homepage quote, Executive Director, Mainframe, Top 5 US Bank: a map verified 100% accurate with the details business analysts needed. 2.0 post: customer evaluations show up to 90% reduction in reverse-engineering time.
tiers.replyDensity: Highest intent. They are already staffing the hardest estate Swimm publishes against.

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: Active stack migration
tiers.trigger: Open req names .NET Framework, WebForms, VB.NET, classic ASP, COM interop, J2EE, EJB, Struts, JSP, WebSphere, WebLogic, monolith-to-microservices, API-first, or headless, and no mainframe keyword
tiers.pain: They are hiring to move the stack. The spec still lives in the code. .NET page: auto-translators stop at 60%, the last 40% is hand work, and that is where projects stall. Java page: Oracle changed the math on Java 8, and the upgrade chain does not end. Monolith page: every deploy is a coordination event. API-first page: business logic has no source of truth across web, mobile, backend, and stored procs.
tiers.valueProp: Product-enabled migration, not a tool license. Deterministic maps first, verified patterns at scale, SMEs on the last 40%. Delivered change is migrated code, extracted services, API contracts, and parity evidence. Java and monolith pages: starting at 1M lines of code. Fixed-price stages, no open-ended T&M.
tiers.replyDensity: Strong. They already budgeted a role to move off the named stack.

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: AI coding-tool keyword
tiers.trigger: Open req names GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code, MCP, or AI coding assistant, and no mainframe or migration keyword
tiers.pain: They already bought the assistant. AI-ready page: Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code adoption is flat because suggestions are wrong or generic. The tools are only as smart as the context you feed them. Filenames and READMEs are not enough for internal agents or MCP servers.
tiers.valueProp: Agentic context layer: deterministic maps, documented flows, SME tribal knowledge, exposed via MCP and wired into Copilot, Cursor, and Claude Code. SwimmBench blog: average Claude Code response time savings of 75% and average cost savings of 61% versus native exploration, tested on a nearly 5 million line codebase. 2.0 post repeats 75% time and 61% cost when agents work from Swimm's understanding layer versus raw code.
tiers.replyDensity: Good. They already pay for the assistant Swimm says is stuck without a knowledge base.

tiers.name: Catch-all
tiers.label: Remaining TAM
tiers.trigger: Every remaining in-TAM engineering org: visible CTO / VP Eng / Head of Architecture / CIO or software-engineer jobs, and none of the keywords above
tiers.pain: They are still in the engineering set Swimm sells into. The codebase is still opaque. AI tools and modernization wait on the same undocumented system. Maya's original pitch is this gap: modernize the codebase for AI readiness.
tiers.valueProp: Assessment is the entry: snapshot of the stack and AI-readiness gap, scoped plan, risks, success criteria. Then a knowledge base, migrated code, or extracted APIs, whichever the offering scopes. Homepage: 100M+ lines of code analyzed. SOC 2, ISO 27001, on-prem including air-gapped, customer-managed LLMs. Fixed price per stage.
tiers.dataSource: LinkedIn TAM after higher tiers route out
tiers.replyDensity: Broadest coverage. Softest ask. Still 100% of TAM.

campaigns.name: Migration Pattern Map
campaigns.strategy: Name {{migration_stack}} in the open req, then offer deterministic maps plus verified patterns for the last 40% auto-translators miss
campaigns.overview: The .NET / Java / monolith / API-first majority. Stack name is a merge tag, not a campaign split.

campaigns.name: Fixed-price Assessment variant
campaigns.strategy: Keep {{migration_stack}} in the first line. Lead with Assessment as a scoped, fixed-price entry and no open-ended T&M.
campaigns.overview: A/B against the pattern map. Same exclusive route, commercial language instead of last-40% language.

campaigns.name: Copilot Context-Gap One-Pager
campaigns.strategy: Name {{ai_tool}} in the req and the flat-adoption line from the AI-ready page, then offer the MCP knowledge base
campaigns.overview: The Copilot / Cursor / Claude Code majority. Context-gap side of the A/B.

campaigns.name: 75 / 61 SwimmBench variant
campaigns.strategy: Keep {{ai_tool}} in the first line. Lead with 75% faster and 61% cheaper Claude Code queries from the SwimmBench blog.
campaigns.overview: A/B against the one-pager. Same waterfall tier, token-cost hook. Do not quote the blog's hypothetical 200-developer math as a Swimm result.

campaigns.name: AI-Readiness Assessment Snapshot
campaigns.filter: Remaining in-TAM engineering orgs, job_keyword_class = none
campaigns.strategy: Notice the engineering org LinkedIn already lists, name the opaque-codebase gap Maya pitched, offer the Assessment snapshot Swimm already sells as stage 01
campaigns.overview: Catch-all coverage so every scraped engineering org still gets one route. Assessment is the tiny yes.

campaigns.name: No-flag-day starter
campaigns.strategy: Lead with one-capability-at-a-time, old paths running until parity, on-prem and air-gapped. Do not change routing.
campaigns.overview: A/B against the snapshot. Still exclusive catch-all, still one TAM.

launchPlan: Pull LinkedIn Sales Nav for engineering organizations with a visible CTO, VP Engineering, Head of Architecture, Head of Platform, Head of Modernization, CIO, or software-engineer jobs. Keep the open-req keyword in the same export. Classify job_keyword_class as mainframe, migration, ai_coding, or none. Suppress already_customer when a Swimm deployment is visible. Do not apply an unpublished headcount or 1M-LOC list cutoff; Java and monolith pages use 1M LOC as delivery scope, not a scrape filter.
Resolve work emails in Apollo only after the domain is routed. Title is a merge tag, not a second TAM.
Launch Tier 1 Mainframe Parity Brief first. Smallest list, sharpest estate signal. Save-time / 90% reverse-engineering copy as the control, Claude Code 35/70/42 as the A/B on the same list.
Add Tier 2 Migration Pattern Map once {{migration_stack}} merge tags are clean across .NET, Java, monolith, and API-first keywords. Then Tier 3 Copilot Context-Gap.

Turn on the AI-Readiness Assessment Snapshot catch-all last so every remaining in-TAM engineering org still has a route. Keep industry as a merge tag, not a campaign split, until one job-keyword tier is clearly working. Do not launch a tier under about 1,500 contacts; that threshold is the SOP, not a Swimm site number.

thresholds.action: Perfect. Scale that tier. Keep the winning time, parity, cost, or context variant.
Good. Let it run. Do not mix a non-engineering TAM into this waterfall.

thresholds.action: Cut that copy variant. Keep the exclusive waterfall.
